caseno:
Civil Revision No. 1482 of 2012
With
Civil Revision No. 1441 of 2012
lawyer:
Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed with Mr. Moudud Ahmed with Mr. Syed Md. Tajrul Hossain with Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali with Mr. Muhammad Tajul Islam, Advocates ------ For the petitioners
Mr. Md. Mokhlesur Rahman, Advocate ------ For the opposite party No.1
Mr. Mahbubey Alam, Attorney General with Mr. Delwar Hossain, D.A.G. with Mr. Bhobesh Chandra Sarker, D.A.G., ------ For the opposite party No.2
parties:
Nur Jahan Begum and others
Vs.
Syed Ahmed Hashmi and others
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal, J: Both these Rules were taken op for hearing together as both the Rules arose from the judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 (decree signed on 11.01.2012) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.619 of 1999 reversing those dated 31.8.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 are being disposed of by this common judgment.

2. These Rules were issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 passed in Title Appeal No.619 and 709 of 1999 by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka reversing those dated 31.8.1999 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. Facts of the ease, in brief, are that Md. Abu Patch Bhuiyan the predecessor of the petitioners herein as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.653 of 1980 in the Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Court, Dhaka against the defendant-opposite party for declaration of title. The said suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer as Title Suit No.360 of 1985 again the suit was renumbered on transfer before the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka as Title Suit No.77 of 1993.

4. Plaintiff's case, in-short, is that:

That the property fully described in the schedule hereinafter called the suit property originally, belonged to one Syed Ahmed Hashmi son of Hazi Ahmed of 71, Circuit House, Daily Road, Dhaka, the defendant No. 1 who became the owner of the same by way of allotment from the then Dhaka Improvement Trust by Allotment Letter No.2444 dated 26.3.1962 for a valuable consideration of Tk.I0,219/- only and accordingly he had been owning and possessing the suit property peacefully and exclusively without any hindrance from the quarter.

5. That the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi while owner in possession of the suit property in the manner aforesaid by exercising all rights of ownership and on payment of rent to the ex-land-lord in his name, the plaintiff went in to possessions of the suit property in the middle of May, 1962 and since then the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit property adversely against the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi and all other and constructed structures in some portion of the suit property and constructed boundary wall by his owls money and for his own interest and has been living thereon with all the members of his family and letting out some portion of the house to monthly eject able tenants without any hindrance or disturbance from any quarter.

6. That the plaintiff during his long peaceful and undisturbed possession since 1962 developed the suit property by spending huge amount of money and also paid rents of the suit property in his name enjoyed the profits and dealt wills the suit property openly and adversely against all others including the defendants and the plaintiff also installed the Electric and Sewerage connection in the suit property.

7. That while owning and possessing in the manner aforesaid the S.A. operation started in the area, the settlement staff surveyed the suit premises and assigned the new S.A. plot and recorded the same in the name of the plaintiff finding him in actual physical possession and on examination of his papers, but after final publication of S.A. record the plaintiff found to his utter surprise that the suit premises was wrongly recorded in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi, the plaintiff tried his best to corrects the S.A. record in his name but could not do so as all the stages of correction of S.A. record was then over. But the plaintiff has been paying rents and taxes to the Government in respect of the suit premises in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi as marfatder and had not been facing any disturbance in reaped of his peaceful possession of the suit property.

8. That in the recent R.S. operation the settlement Amin Sureveyed the suit premises and assigned the new R.S. plot and recorded the same in the name of the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi the defendant No.1 wrongly and through mistake. An objection under Rule 30 was filed by the plaintiff in the settlement department for correction of the R.S. record in his name.

9. That the plaintiff has been paying rent and taxes of the suit premises to the Government and living therein with all the members of his family without any hindrance from any quarter, the plaintiff as such acquired good title over the suit premises by adverse possession having been in peaceful and undisturbed possession for more than 12 (twelve) years.

10. That the defendant No.2 who has got no right, title, interest and possession of the suit property, with a view to grab the suit property has been giving out in the locality that he has purchased the suit property from the defendant No. 1 and with this end and view lie will enter into the suit property on a good opportunity moment by force and take possession of the same and the defendant No.2 is very dangerous and notorious type of man in the society and is also bad reported man in the area and none will dare to protest against the malafide activities of the defendant No.2 out of fear of life.

11. That the defendant No.2 on 25.6.1980 at about 11 A.M. accompanied by other bad type of men in the locality attempted to enter into the suit property by force and gave out in the locality that he purchased the suit property from the defendant No.1, but due to timely intervention of the plaintiff and his men, the defendant No. 2 could not succeed in his nefarious activities an due to this a cloud has been cast upon the indefeasible right, title and interest to the plaintiff in respect of the suit property and to remove the cloud so cast a declaration of plaintiffs title from the Court in respect of the suit property is essential and as such the plaintiff has filed this suit.

12. Defendant, Syed Ahmed Hashmi contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that:

13. That the addresses of the plaintiff mentio0ned in the plaint are wrong and the plaintiff has no right and ownership in the suit property. The said plaintiff is the tenant of the defendant in the suit property at Tk.400/-.

14. That the suit property previously owned and possessed by the RAJUK and thereafter the RAJUK allotted the said suit property to the defendant paid all dues to the RAJUK.

15. That the defendant has been possessing and residing in the suit property building house therein and the suit property was recorded in the name of the defendant in the S.A. and R.S. Khatain and the defendant has been possessing the same by paying rent and khazna of the suit property.

16. That the defendant ranted the suit property to the plaintiff and made an agreement in this respect. The plaintiff was not paying the rent regularly.

17. Defendant No.3, RAJUK contested the suit by filing written statements, stating, inter-alia,

18. That the land measuring 13 katha 8 chatak situated in Gulshan Model Town. The said Syed Ahmed Hashmi got allotment of the said land on 26.3.1962 and also got building plan on 21.10.1962 but the said Syed Ahmed Hashmi did not construct any building in the suit property according to mid building plan. Thereafter RAJUK got the possession of the suit property by canceling the said building plan.

19. That the defendant No.1 had no citizenship of Bangladesh after 1972. The defendant No.1 had been possessing the said suit property illegally and there was no adverse possession in the suit property.

20. At the trial plaintiff side examined as many as 5 witnesses while one witness namely, defendant No.2 was examined as DW-2 and one witness was examined for and on behalf of defendant RAJUK as DW-1 and both the parties also exhibited some documents to prove their respective cases.

21. After hearing the argument of both the sides an on considering the evidence and materials on record the learned trial Judge, however, decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31.8.1999 (decree signed on 6.9.1999).

22. On appeal being Title Appeal No.619 of 1999 and Tide Appeal No.709 of 1999 the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka by the impugned judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court dated 31.8.1999 passed in Title Suit No.77 of 1993 on the finding that there is no cause of action for filing the suit, the suit is barred by law, the suit is defective, inconsistent and the plaintiff side miserably failed to prove his case.

23. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 4.01.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. No.619 of 1999 and Title Appeal No.709 of 1999 the present petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

24. In this case before entering into the merit of the case, I feel it necessary to mention that Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners obtained both these Rules and while the matter was taken up for hearing Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed retired from the case and thereafter, Mr. Moudud Ahmed along with Mr. Syed Md. Tajrul Hossain filed a fresh power and took adjournment again and again and thereafter, on 02.7.2015 filed an application for call for the records of Title Appeal No.6I9 of 1999 and accordingly after hearing the said application was allowed by order dated 63.2015 and thereafter again the case was made ready for hearing on 5.8.2015 and thereafter on 20.8.2015 on the prayer of Mr. Moudud Ahmed again took adjournment till 26,8,2015 for the last time and on that date Mr. Moudud Ahmed again took adjournment and thereafter on 30.8.2015 Mr. Moudud Ahmed again upon referring an application for calling the record filed on 26.8.2015 submits that to proper adjudication of the matter record from the RAJUK may kindly be called for and after hearing both the sides the said application was kept with the record, as prayed for and on the prayer of Mr. Moudud Ahmed again the matter was adjourned till 6.9.2015 and on 6.9.2015 the matter was again adjourned for two days and thereafter on 8.9.2015 Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam appearing on behalf of the petitioners filed a fresh power and says that Mr. Moudud Ahmed retired from the case and Mr. Tajul Islam, however, most empathically prays for short adjoumment to do the case and thereafter finally on 13.9.2015 Mr. A. J. Mohammad All along with Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam appearing on behalf of the petitioners prays for adjournment the case till re-opening of the forthcoming vacation and after hearing both the sides the further prayer for adjournment is rejected and thereafter Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali or Mr. Mohammad Tajul Islam did not turn to make their submission.

25. In this case Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed and Mr. Moudud Ahmed time to time make the submission although finally without concluding the submission they retired from the case.

26. Mr. Sk. Md. Morshed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in both the Rules after placing the material portion from the judgments of two Courts below and other materials on record submits that the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Dhaka erred in law in setting aside the well founded judgment of the trial Court without properly considering the facts and circumstance of the case and the case made out by the petitioners that the defendant-opposite party No.2, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake party and the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land over a period of 35 years by paying all rents to the Government and as such they are entitled to get adverse possession.

27. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners at one stage, however, submits that the Court of appeal below ought to have considered that fraud vitiates everything as the appellant, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake person, who is not entitled to get any relief whatsoever and thereby fail into an error of law resulting in the error in the, decision occasioning failure of justice.

28. Mr. Mahbubey Alum, the learned Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party-Rajuk in support the Civil Revisions submits that the properly in question owned and possessed by RAJUK and according to law the plaintiff must prove more than 60 years continuous possession in the suit land in order to get adverse decree against the Government but in this case the plaintiff in the plaint taken a plea of getting possession in May, 1962, that is, admittedly below 60 years. Mr. Mahbubey Alam further submits that from a plain reading of the plaint together with the evidence of PW- 1, PW-2, PW-3, PW-4 and PW-5 it is apparent that the plaintiff's suit is incompetent, baseless and frivolous in nature. Mr. Mahbubey Alam in support of his submission has relied on the decision reported in 61 DLR 430.

29. Mr. Bhobesh Chandra Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the defendant-opposite party, RAJUK in the course of his argument after placing the plaint of the case submits that the instant suit is incompetent and vexatious in nature and the plaintiff filed the suit with intent to grab the land. Finally, the learned Deputy Attorney General submits that the Court of appeal below rightly arrived at a finding that the plaintiff side neither prove any case of title nor prove their any ownership and possession in the suit land.

30. Mr. Md. Mokhlesur Rahman (Zahid), the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-opposite party No.1, Syed Ahmed Hashmi proved his ownership in the suit land by adducing evidence both oral and documentary that he got the suit land from RAJUK through lease allotment letter dated 26.3.1962 (Ext.Ta) and subsequently it was registered on 20.8.1962 being deed No.7789 dated 20.8.1962 (Ext.Neo) and tire Court of appeal below as last Court of fact factually found that the defendant Syed Ahmed Hashmi is the real owner of the suit land on getting lease from RAJUK in accordance with law. He further submits that the plea as taken by the plaintiff in the trial Court below that the instant defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi is a fake person false to the ground pursuant to order No.149 dated 19.7.98 passed by the teamed Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman further submits that the plaintiff neither made out a case of adverse possession nor in their evidence although the trial Court below abruptly decreed the suit on the ground of adverse possession and the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact rightly on assigning sound reason arrived at a clear finding that the plaintiff miserably failed to prove their any title in the suit land whatsoever. Finally, Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman submits that the plaintiff's suit is in fact incompetent, baseless, misconceived and the same is not legally tenable in law which is liable to be buried without any further delay for the ends of justice.

31. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the sides and the learned Attorney General and Deputy Attorney General and perused the judgments of two Courts below, deposition of witnesses and other connected papers as filed thereto.

32. Now, to deal with the contention raised by the learned Advocates for the respective parties, I feel it necessary to decide first whether the suit itself was maintainable.

33. To resolve this dispute, I feel it necessary to quote hereunder the prayer portion of the plaint in full extent. Prayer portion of the plaint roads as follows:

34. A decree declaring plaintiff's title over 16 annas share of the suit property.

35. All costs of the suit.

36. Any other ancillary relief of reliefs to which the plaintiff is legally and equitably entitled to.

37. From the above, it transpires that the plaintiff did not make any prayer for a decree of adverse possession.

<u>38. Reading the plaint as a whole, it appears that they entered into the suit land as tenant of defendant No.1, Syed Abased Hashmi and subsequently, they entered into the suit land in the middle part of May, 1962 and since then the plaintiff side owning and possessing the suit land as adversely against their landlord, Syed Ahmed Hashmi.</u>

<u>39. On scrutiny of the record, I do not find any valid ground to suggest that the plaintiff entered into the suit land as tenant under defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi in the middle part of May, 1962.</u>

40. The Court of appeal below as last Court of fact after a detailed discussion of the materials on record came to the conclusion that there was no cause of action to file the suit, the plaintiff's case is not maintainable against RAJUK according to law.

41. In coining to this finding that the said Court observed us follows:-

“বাদীপক্ষ আর্জির কোথায় ৬০ (ষাট) বছরের উর্দ্ধকাল নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে ৩নং বিবাদী ডিআইটি তথা রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের জ্ঞাতসারে বিরুদ্ধ দখলকার রহিয়াছে তাহা উল্লেখ করেন নাই। ……………বাদীর আর্জি পর্যালোচনা করিলে দেখা যায় যে, বাদী রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ বা সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমী অর্থাত যথাক্রমে ১ ও ৩ নং বিবাদী এর বিরুদ্ধে বিরুদ্ধ দখলজনিত স্বত্বের স্বপক্ষে কোন ই্তিহাস বা ঘটনা বা কোন নালিশের কারন বর্ণনা করেন নাই। বাদী যাহার বিরুদ্ধে নালিশের কারন উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন অর্থাত ২নং বিবাদী তিনি এই মোকদ্দমার বিরোধীয় সম্পত্তির লীজদাতা বা লীজগ্রহিতা কেহই নহেন। বাদী ৩য় ব্যক্তি ২ নং বিবাদী এর বিরুদ্ধে নালিশের কারন উদ্ভব দেখাইয়া ১, ২ ও ৩ নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে বিরুদ্ধ দখলজনিত স্বত্বের দাবী করিয়াছেন।…………….. যেহেতু ল অব এ্যাডভার্স পজেশন এর বিধান মোতাবেক কোন ঘচনা আর্জিতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই্, কোন ঘটনার ভিত্তিতে, কিভাবে, কখন, কোথায় এই প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমীর সম্পত্তি জবরদখল করিয়াছিলেন এবং উক্তরূপ জবর দখল প্রকৃত হাশমীর জ্ঞাত ছিল তথাপিও প্রকৃত হাশমী বাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দীর্ঘ ১২ বছরে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহন করেন নাই, বাদী জোরপূর্বক হাশমীর জ্ঞাতসারে নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে ভোগ দখলকার রহিয়াছে তদ্রুপ কোন ইতিহাস বা ঘটনা আর্জিতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই, সেহেতু আর্জিতে মূল মোকদ্দমা উদ্ভবের যে কারন উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন তাহা প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমী বা রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের কোন স্বার্থ ক্ষুন্ন হয় নাই। এই মোকদ্দমা দায়েরে বাদীপক্ষের কোন নালিশের কারন উদ্ভবন হয় নাই। এই মোকদ্দমার ঘটনা ও বর্ণনা মোতাবেক রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে আইনের বিধান মোতাবেক অচল। এই মোকদ্দমার প্রকৃত সৈয়দ আহম্মেদ হাশমীর বিরুদ্ধে কোন নালিশের কারন বিদ্যমান নাই।”

42. These are being purely findings of fact based on proper appreciation of fact and law.

43. I find no flaw in the reasonings of the Court of appeal below. The learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka appears to have considered all the legal aspects of the case and justly set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

44. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstance of the case, it appears that the plaintiff's suit is incompetent, frivolous, misconceived and barred by law as well.

45. However, in view of the papers, lease deeds, exhibits, city survey and admitted facts it is desirable that the defendant-opposite party, RAJUK will do the needful in favour of the defendant-opposite party, Syed Ahmed Hashmi.

46. I want to address the question raised by the plaintiff side that the present Syed Ahmed Hashmi is not a genuine Syed Ahmed Hashmi.

47. In this connection, I like to quote hereunder the material portion of the order No.149 dated 19.7.1998 which reads as follows:

“১নং বিবাদী সৈয়দ আহম্মদ হাসমি তাহা প্রমানের নিমিত্তে ১নং বিবাদির বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী ফিরিস্তি যোগে ১ নং বিবাদীর ফটো সম্বলিত যুগ্ন সচিব, মন্ত্রি পরিষদ বিভাগ কর্তৃক ১৪/৬/৯৮ ইং তারিখের জাতীয়তা সনদপত্র প্রথম শ্রেনীর ম্যাজিষ্ট্রেট কর্তৃক ২/৯/৮৯ ও ৩০/৯/৭৩ ইং তারিখের হলফনামার ফটোবপি দাখিল করে বিধায় আপাতঃ দৃষ্টিতে আদালতের নিকট প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, আদালতে স্বয়ং উপস্থিত সৈয়দ আহম্মদ হাসমি-ই ১নং বিবাদী হিসাবে মোকদ্দমায় প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করিতেছে।”

48. In view of my discussion made in the foregoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant Rules must fail.

49. In the result, both the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

50. Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.
